extracted.intended_audience: Florida state agencies, agency attorneys, administrative law judges, regulated persons, and administrative practitioners involved in rulemaking, petitions for variances/waivers, and rule challenges
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory standards and procedural requirements in Florida's Administrative Procedure Act governing petitions for variances/waivers, agency rule review, committee review, publication, summary removal, and challenges to rules or unadopted statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules on variances and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration Commission shall adopt uniform rules of procedure under s. 120.54(5) establishing procedures for granting or denying petitions for variances and waivers, including emergency and temporary variances and waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform rules must include procedures for granting, denying, or revoking emergency and temporary variances and waivers. Such provisions may provide for expedited timeframes, waiver of or limited public notice, and limitations on comments on the petition in the case of such temporary or emergency variances and waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to advise and provide materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall advise persons of the remedies available through this section and shall provide copies of this section, the uniform rules on variances and waivers, and, if requested, the underlying statute to persons who inquire about relief from rule requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must supply requested statutory and procedural materials to inquirers about possible relief from rule requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition contents for variance or waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition for a variance or waiver shall specify: (a) the rule from which relief is requested; (b) the type of action requested; (c) the specific facts that would justify a waiver or variance for the petitioner; and (d) the reason why the variance or waiver would serve the purposes of the underlying statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to any uniform rule requirements, petitions must include these four elements to be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and comment on variance/waiver petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days after receipt of a petition for variance or waiver, an agency shall provide notice of the petition to the Department of State, which shall publish notice in the first available issue of the Florida Administrative Register; the notice must include petitioner name, filing date, rule number and nature, and how to obtain a copy of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform rules shall provide a means for interested persons to provide comments on the petition. Emergency/temporary petitions may be subject to expedited notice or limited comment as authorized by the uniform rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review timelines and processing rules for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for emergency requests, within 30 days after receipt of a petition an agency shall review it and may request additional information; within 30 days after receipt of additional information the agency may request only clarifying information; agencies shall grant or deny within 90 days after receipt of the timely requested original petition, additional material, or petitioner’s written request to finish processing; petitions not decided within 90 days after receipt of a completed petition are deemed approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petitioner asserts a request for additional information is unauthorized, the agency shall proceed, at petitioner's written request, to process the petition. A copy of the order granting or denying must contain statement of relevant facts and reasons and be filed with the committee. Agency decisions must be supported by competent substantial evidence and are subject to ss. 120.569 and 120.57. Agencies must maintain records of type and disposition of each petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rule review schedule and reporting obligations (120.5435)
rubrics_metrics.description: By July 1, 2030, each agency, in coordination with the committee, must review all existing rules adopted before July 1, 2025; beginning Oct 1, 2025, agencies must include a list of existing rules in their annual regulatory plan and a schedule to review at least 20% of rules per year until reviewed; rules adopted after July 1, 2025 must be reviewed in the fifth year following adoption and completed before the sixth year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subsection implementing this schedule stands repealed July 1, 2032. Agencies must submit an annual report by January 1 summarizing intended actions on each rule under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule review substantive criteria (120.5435(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency rule review must determine whether each rule: (a) is a valid exercise of delegated legislative authority; (b) has current statutory authority; (c) reiterates or paraphrases statutory material; (d) is in proper form; (e) is consistent with expressed legislative intent regarding the provisions the rule implements; (f) requires a technical or substantive update to reflect current use; and (g) requires updated references to statutory citations and incorporated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must assess each of these seven factors and include the assessment in their submissions when they determine no change or make technical changes; substantive changes require following full chapter procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency actions & submission requirements following rule review
rubrics_metrics.description: After rule review an agency shall take one of: (a) make no change; (b) make a technical change; (c) make a substantive change; or (d) repeal the rule. Each option has specific submission and publication requirements (deadlines by April 1) and differing susceptibility to challenge as a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no change is necessary, submit reviewed rule, written statement of intended action, and assessment of factors specified in subsection (4) by April 1 — not subject to challenge as a proposed rule under s.120.56(2). For technical changes, submit reviewed rule and recommended technical changes coded, written statement, assessment, and facts justifying change by April 1 — not subject to challenge. For substantive changes, make all changes per chapter, publish a notice of rule development in FAR by April 1, and submit reviewed rule and coded recommended changes plus written statement and assessment by April 1 (submission to committee is not itself a notice of rule development). For repeal, repeal per chapter and publish required notice in FAR by April 1 and submit written statement and assessment by April 1 (submission is not a notice of proposed rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee review scope (120.545)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee shall examine each proposed rule (with limited statutory exemptions), each emergency rule, each rule reviewed under 120.5435, and may examine any existing rule and accompanying interpreting material to determine whether the rule satisfies enumerated statutory and policy considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This examination is a legislative check on delegated authority and applies to proposed, emergency, and reviewed rules as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee review criteria (120.545(1)(a)-(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee evaluates whether: (a) the rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority; (b) the statutory authority has been repealed; (c) the rule reiterates or paraphrases statutory material; (d) the rule is in proper form; (e) the prior notice was sufficient to explain purpose and effect; (f) the rule is consistent with expressed legislative intent for the specific law implemented; (g) the rule is necessary to accomplish the objectives of the law; (h) the rule is a reasonable implementation as it affects convenience of the public or persons particularly affected; (i) the rule could be made less complex or more comprehensible; (j) the rule’s statement of estimated regulatory costs complies with s.120.541 and whether less costly alternatives could substantially accomplish statutory objectives; (k) the rule will require additional appropriations; (l) for emergency rules, whether there exists an emergency and the agency complied with s.120.54(4); and (m) the rule includes a provision not authorized by statute that automatically expires or is repealed on a specific date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may request reasonably necessary information from agencies and consult legislative standing committees with subject jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee objection process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the committee objects to a rule, it must, within 5 days after the objection, certify that fact to the agency and include a detailed statement of objections; the committee shall notify legislative leaders concurrently and include a copy of the rule and the objection statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receipt of an objection, the agency (if headed by an individual) has 30 days, or (if headed by a collegial body) 45 days to respond and must choose among specified options depending on whether the rule is in effect or not. Failure to respond within prescribed time for a rule not yet in effect constitutes withdrawal of the rule; failure to respond for a rule in effect constitutes a refusal to amend or repeal the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response options to committee objection (120.545(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the prescribed period after receipt of committee objection the agency shall: if rule is not yet in effect — (1) file notice of necessary modifications, (2) file notice of withdrawal, or (3) notify committee it refuses to modify or withdraw; if rule is in effect — (1) file notice to amend without prior notice of rule development, (2) file notice to repeal, or (3) notify committee it refuses to amend or repeal. If objection concerns estimated regulatory costs, agency may (1) prepare corrected statement and publish availability or (2) notify committee it refuses to prepare a corrected statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different filing mechanisms are specified (e.g., s.120.54(3)(d) or s.120.54(3)(a)). The agency's written notifications and filings must comply with chapter requirements and timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of agency refusal or failure to respond and committee remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to respond as required may constitute withdrawal or refusal as described; if the committee objects and the agency refuses to take required action, the committee shall file with the Department of State a notice of objection which will be published in the Florida Administrative Register. If the agency fails to act in good faith to modify/withdraw/repent, the committee may recommend legislation to address the objection and may request temporary suspension of the rule or proposed rule pending legislative consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If committee requests temporary suspension and agency does not suspend within statutory time, agency may be deemed to have refused; a suspended rule may not be the basis for agency action during suspension but remains subject to administrative and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Florida Administrative Code and Register (120.55(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of State shall compile and publish electronically the Florida Administrative Code (official compilation) and the Florida Administrative Register, containing all required materials, text of proposed rules, notices of public meetings/hearings/workshops, petitions, and other specified items. The electronic code is the official compilation; department retains copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain local or internal rules may be excluded from the Code without affecting validity. The Department may contract for printed publication but retains responsibility. History notes must reflect rule review completion and technical changes must be published as notices of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Administrative Register contents & public access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register must include all notices required by s.120.54(2) and (3)(a) showing text of proposed rules, notices of meetings/hearings with statement of how to obtain agendas, notices of uniform rule changes, petitions for declaratory statements/administrative determinations, lists of untimely reviewed rules, summaries of committee objections, lists of rules filed for adoption, full text of emergency rules in effect, and other authorized material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Register website must allow search by type/date/rule/word/subject/agency, provide a 5-year searchable archive, offer automated e-mail notification subscriptions with summary text, allow viewing of forms and incorporated materials, allow commenting on proposed rules, and make access and notification services free to the public. Publication on the Register does not preclude agency publication elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and incorporation by reference standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms may not be published in the Florida Administrative Code, but any form used by an agency in dealings with the public and meeting the statutory definition of 'rule' must be filed with the committee before use and incorporated by reference in the appropriate rule with number, title, effective date, and explanation of how the form may be obtained. After Dec 31, 2025, incorporated materials must be filed in prescribed electronic manner; hyperlinks in the Code may only point to material filed with and maintained by the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a form is incorporated after Dec 31, 2007 via rule notice, it must clearly display number, title, effective date, and rule number. Department's publication must hyperlink from the rule to incorporated material filed electronically with the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary removal (summary repeal) procedure for rules no longer in force (120.555)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Department of State doubts whether a rule is still in force, it shall request a written statement from the agency head or Governor and publish notice in the Register; the agency/Governor must respond within 90 days stating whether the rule is in effect; failure to respond constitutes acknowledgment the rule is no longer in effect and subject to summary repeal; notice of the response/acknowledgment is published and, if rule is not in effect or no response, the notice gives 21 days to file an objection as a petition under s.120.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections to summary repeal must be filed within 21 days naming the appropriate respondent (agency or Dept. of State if no agency has authority); if no timely objection or if a decision finding rule not in effect becomes final, the Department shall remove the rule and provide historical notes describing manner of cessation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General procedures for challenging rules (120.56(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person substantially affected by a rule or proposed rule may seek an administrative determination of invalidity on the ground the rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority. The petition must state the particular provisions alleged invalid and grounds, and facts sufficient to show the petitioner is substantially affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be filed electronically with the division which forwards copies to the agency, Dept. of State, and committee. If petition complies, within 10 days the division director assigns an administrative law judge who shall conduct a hearing within 30 days unless withdrawn or continuance granted. Failure of an agency to follow applicable rulemaking procedures is presumed material but may be rebutted by the agency by showing petitioner’s substantial interests and fairness not impaired. Within 30 days after the hearing the ALJ shall render a written decision and transmit copies to agency, Dept. of State, and committee. Hearings are de novo, standard of proof is preponderance of the evidence, and the ALJ's order is final agency action; other substantially affected persons may intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for challenging proposed rules (120.56(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition alleging invalidity of a proposed rule must be filed within specified windows (e.g., within 21 days after publication of notice required by s.120.54(3)(a); within 10 days after final public hearing; within 20 days after SERC prepared/made available; or within 20 days after publication required by s.120.54(3)(d)). Petitioner bears burden to prove substantial affectation; agency bears burden to prove by preponderance that proposed rule is not invalid exercise of delegated authority as to objections raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ALJ may declare proposed rule wholly or partly invalid; unless reversed on appeal, invalid provisions shall not be adopted. After a petition is filed, agency may proceed with other rulemaking steps; if part of proposed rule declared invalid, agency may withdraw entire proposed rule. Agency must give notice of the ALJ decision in the first available Register issue. A proposed rule challenged under this section is not presumed valid or invalid when a substantially affected person seeks invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for challenging existing rules in effect (120.56(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition alleging invalidity of an existing rule may be filed at any time while the rule is in effect. The petitioner has the burden to prove by preponderance that the existing rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority as to the objections raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ALJ may declare all or part invalid; the invalid portion becomes void when appeals period expires. The agency must give notice of the decision in the Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging agency statements defined as unadopted rules (120.56(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person substantially affected by an agency statement that is an unadopted rule may seek an administrative determination that the statement violates s.120.54(1)(a). The petition shall include the text or description and facts sufficient to show the statement is an unadopted rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ALJ may extend hearing beyond 30 days for good cause. If the agency publishes a notice of rulemaking under s.120.54(3), such notice automatically stays proceedings pending adoption unless the ALJ vacates the stay. If petitioner proves allegations at hearing, the agency has burden to prove that rulemaking is not feasible or practicable under s.120.54(1)(a). The ALJ may determine whether all or part of a statement violates s.120.54(1)(a); the decision is a final order and will be transmitted to the Dept. of State for publication.
